question: What is the primary definition of asepsis in healthcare?

options.A: The reduction of visible dust on surfaces
options.B: The chemical destruction of skin tissues
options.C: The total absence of disease-producing microorganisms
options.D: The complete elimination of all water sources

explanation: Asepsis literally means free from infection or contaminating microorganisms. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h1)

question: Hospital-acquired infections are also commonly referred to by what name?
explanation: Infections that originate or develop within a hospital or healthcare facility are termed nosocomial infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h1)

question: Medical asepsis is best described by which term?
explanation: Medical asepsis involves practices that reduce the number and transfer of pathogens, commonly known as clean technique. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h2)

question: When is surgical asepsis strictly required during routine nursing tasks?
explanation: Catheter insertion enters a sterile body cavity, requiring full surgical asepsis to prevent introducing bacteria. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h2)

question: An environment where a pathogen can live and multiply is called what?
explanation: A reservoir provides a suitable habitat for microorganisms to grow, multiply, and survive. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h3)

question: Handwashing primarily breaks which link in the chain of infection?
explanation: Washing hands removes transient microbes, preventing them from transferring from one surface or person to another. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections?
explanation: Frequent and proper handwashing or sanitizing removes pathogens before they can spread. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h4)

question: Standard precautions must be used for which category of hospital patients?

options.A: All patients in the healthcare setting
options.C: Patients admitted to surgical wards only

explanation: Standard precautions apply universally to care for every patient to minimize unseen transmission risks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h4)

question: What part of a sterile drape is considered contaminated by default?

options.A: The exact center of the field
options.C: The bottom surface facing the tray

explanation: The outer edge touches unsterile surfaces during setup, making the outer one-inch margin contaminated. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why does moisture cause a sterile field to become contaminated?

options.A: Water changes the chemical pH of sterile instruments
options.B: It allows bacteria to move through the barrier via capillary action
options.C: Moisture attracts dust particles from the room ventilation
options.D: Wet packages instantly dissolve surgical steel

explanation: Liquid creates a bridge that pulls microorganisms through porous sterile wrappers from non-sterile surfaces. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which process completely eliminates all microbial life, including bacterial spores?
explanation: Sterilization is the only process that destroys every form of microbial life, including tough spores. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of cleaning instruments before disinfection or sterilization?

options.A: To cool down items that were heated in storage
options.B: To remove organic material that can block germicidal action
options.C: To polish the stainless steel surfaces for better grip
options.D: To ensure the equipment smells clean for patients

explanation: Blood, tissue, and debris protect microorganisms from disinfectants, so cleaning must happen first. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h6)

question: What should a nurse do immediately if a break in sterile technique occurs?

options.A: Ask the patient if they noticed any dirty tools
options.B: Take corrective action and replace the contaminated item
options.C: Wait until the procedure ends to report the incident
options.D: Ignore it if the item only touched a clean glove

explanation: Integrity of the sterile field must be maintained; contaminated items must be replaced immediately. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h7)

question: How does the nurse directly protect vulnerable patients through asepsis?

options.A: By locking room doors to keep visitors away permanently
options.B: By consistently practicing proper hand hygiene and barrier techniques
options.C: By prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every new admission
options.D: By wiping down walls with bleach solution hourly

explanation: Consistent application of aseptic habits stops pathogens from reaching susceptible patients. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h7)
